name: apple-vision-mcp
description: OCR images and scanned PDFs through Vision's text recognition
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift for optical character recognition: reads text out of an image (PNG, JPEG, HEIC, TIFF…) or out of a scanned PDF, page by page, through Vision's VNRecognizeTextRequest.

For a PDF, PDFKit is used only to rasterize each page into a bitmap — this server never reads a PDF's own text layer, outline or metadata. That is apple-pdf-mcp's job, and it is faster and more accurate whenever a PDF actually has a text layer. Try pdf_read first on any PDF; vision_ocr is what reads the scan pdf_read cannot.

The folder list below is the ONE deliberate exception to "nothing to configure" in this family of extensions: it is the security boundary itself, not a preference, so there is no sensible default to hardcode in its place. Leaving it blank means reading nothing; guessing one would mean guessing what may be exposed.

This server never writes anything and has no delete of any kind.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: vision_status
tools.description: Reports which folders this server may read and whether macOS is actually letting it reach them. Reads no file contents.

tools.name: vision_ocr
tools.description: Runs Vision's text recognition over an image (PNG, JPEG, HEIC, TIFF…) or over a PDF, rendering each page first. Returns the recognised lines in reading order.

read_roots.title: Folders Claude may read
read_roots.description: Claude can run OCR on any image or PDF inside these. Nothing outside them is reachable.
